sbx run <<'EOF'
cd /workspace && ls -la && file * 2>/dev/null; echo '---'; find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -printf '%p %s bytes\n'

xxd main.db | head -40

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('main.db-wal')
data=p.read_bytes()
dec=bytes(b^0x42 for b in data)
Path('main.db-wal.dec').write_bytes(dec)
print(dec[:32].hex())
print('magic', dec[:4].hex(), 'ver', int.from_bytes(dec[4:8],'big'), 'pagesize', int.from_bytes(dec[8:12],'big'))
# detect frames
ps=int.from_bytes(dec[8:12],'big')
print('len',len(dec),'frames',(len(dec)-32)//(24+ps))
for i in range((len(dec)-32)//(24+ps)):
    off=32+i*(24+ps)
    print(i, off, dec[off:off+24].hex())

echo '--- try sqlite with dec wal ---'
cp main.db main_test.db
cp main.db-wal.dec main_test.db-wal

 print(c.execute("select * from items order by id").fetchall())

ls -la

python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json, sqlite3
# Fix the corrupted/encrypted WAL in place (XOR 0x42 obfuscation)
wal = Path('main.db-wal')
data = wal.read_bytes()
fixed = bytes(b ^ 0x42 for b in data)
wal.write_bytes(fixed)
# Read all data, including WAL frames
con = sqlite3.connect('main.db')
rows = con.execute('SELECT id, name, value FROM items ORDER BY id').fetchall()
con.close()
out = [{'id': r[0], 'name': r[1], 'value': r[2]} for r in rows]
Path('recovered.json').write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2) + '\n')
print(json.dumps(out))
print('count:', len(out))
